clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old male initially presented with mild thrombocytopenia and was found on follow-up to have splenomegaly by ultrasound and symptoms of fatigue. Bone marrow biopsy performed about 3 weeks after initial study revealed normocellular marrow with a 30-40% B-cell infiltrate composed of medium sized mature cells with cytoplasmic projections. Immunohistochemistry showed B cells positive for CD20, Annexin A1, DBA44, BCL1, BCL2, TRAP, and BRAF V600E mutation, and negative for CD5, CD10, LEF1, and BCL6. Bone marrow aspirate showed a lymphocyte population of 34%, with B-cells constituting 41% of lymphocytes. Flow cytometry confirmed the B-cell population was positive for CD19, CD20, CD22, HLA-DR, FMC7, and kappa monoclonal, partially positive for CD25 and CD103, consistent with a clonal hairy cell population, confirming the diagnosis of Hairy Cell Leukemia.
